messages.author: 845163828b49c4ca
messages.subject: Calling Genotypes after ACC+QN Normalization
parts:
I'm working on calling genotypes with the Brlmm-p algorithm, which is
part of the Affymetrix APT toolset. I've run into a couple of
problems that are hindering my ability to call reliable genotypes: (1)
small number of samples per batch (2) wide variance across various
sample batches.

In trying to minimize this variance, I've processed the original .CEL
files through ACC and QN Normalization functions of the Aroma
package. After running it through the Aroma pipeline and looking at
some of quality assessment statistics, things look great. The problem
is that Brlmm-p will no longer process the new .CEL files.
Specifically, it doesn't like the negative intensities contained in
the new Aroma .CEL files.

I was thinking of doing something additive to make all intensities
positive but I'm not sure what effect this will have on the calling
function. Can anyone suggest an alternative approach? Or, is there
another calling package available that may work better with output
from Aroma?

Thanks in advance.
Andy

On Tue, May 20, 2008 at 7:36 AM, areynolds <arey...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm working on calling genotypes with the Brlmm-p algorithm, which is
> part of the Affymetrix APT toolset. I've run into a couple of
> problems that are hindering my ability to call reliable genotypes: (1)
> small number of samples per batch (2) wide variance across various
> sample batches.
>
> In trying to minimize this variance, I've processed the original .CEL
> files through ACC and QN Normalization functions of the Aroma
> package. After running it through the Aroma pipeline and looking at
> some of quality assessment statistics, things look great.

> The problem
> is that Brlmm-p will no longer process the new .CEL files.
> Specifically, it doesn't like the negative intensities contained in
> the new Aroma .CEL files.

>
> I was thinking of doing something additive to make all intensities
> positive but I'm not sure what effect this will have on the calling
> function. Can anyone suggest an alternative approach? Or, is there
> another calling package available that may work better with output
> from Aroma?

So, in the bigger picture, downstream methods (that models the
logarithm of the signals) have to decide on how to deal with
non-positive signals. Note that I write "non-positive" and not
"negative", because we might have zeros as well. We should expect
non-positive in SNP data, because for genotypes AA and BB, ideally we
have all zero signals for Allele B and Allele A, respectively.
Indeed, 50% of the genotypes are expected to be AA or BB, so the
expected number of zero probe signals in also 50%. Now, add noise to
this and it is not hard to imagine that the observed values are
negative as well. If you assume symmetric noise, half of the signals
will be negative and half positive (for AA and BB). Thus, typically
you see 25% negative (non-positive) signals if the calibration works
well.

There are various ways to handle non-positive signals if you want to
pass them down to existing methods (based on the log transform). One
can filter the signals such that all PM <= 0 as flagged as missing
(NAs). An alternative is to censor the data such they are all set to
zero (or a small positive value). Another alternative is to translate
the data such that less or no probe signals are non-positive. The
advantage with the latter is that if you shift the data the same
amount for all arrays you know that you have the same systematic
effect in all arrays and multi-chip methods such as BRLMM (and CRLMM)
gain from that. All these approaches are likely to give biases in the
estimates, but that might be the price you have to pay if you want to
use log-models. Of the three, I'd say shift the data (but maybe you
have to accept some negatives in order not to shift too much), because
BRLMM/CRLMM should handle such data "alright".

Having said all this, I would suggest that you post a message on
Affymetrix forum about adding support for non-positive signals in
APT/BRLMM, e.g. handling as missing values, censoring, or shifting. A
genotyping software should handle such cases. They are good (and busy)
guys there and I'm sure they consider it.

You can of course also shift the data using aroma.affymetrix. There
is no ready class for this, but ScaleNormalization takes argument
'shift' and then rescales the signals to the same average across
arrays, which is roughly what AllelicCrosstalkCalibration does, so at
least (to a fairly good I guess) approximately you could use
ScaleNormalization for your purpose.

See also if you can use CRLMM in oligo. [It's on the todo list to
incorporate an aroma.affymetrix API for this, but yet to be done].

Let us know how it goes - I'm quite interested in the outcome. If
you're willing to write up a vignette or similar that would be great.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Thanks in advance.
> Andy

messages.author: 845163828b49c4ca
messages.subject: Re: Calling Genotypes after ACC+QN Normalization
parts:
Hi Henrik,
I figured I’d touch base about my initial inquiry and ask you a couple
follow up questions. I should have noted during my initial
correspondence that the dataset was generated using V2 of the custom
dog array (http://www.broad.mit.edu/mammals/dog/).

I took your suggestion and shifted the intensities by the lowest non-
positive value but things don’t look much better after generating
calls with the new .CEL files. I’m in the middle of assessing if I’ve
indeed shifted “too much” and what would be the optimal shifting
value. I’ve contacted the affymetrix development team and they say
that the brlmm-p algorithm doesn’t support negative values.

A couple questions:
1. Given that this is a custom array, I’ve had no success getting
CRLMM to work for genotype calling; do you know if there are other
alternative calling methods for these types of custom arrays?

2. I’m using the Fusion com library provided by Affymetrix to read the
contents of Affy cel files. After running ACC+QN there are a handful
of files that I can no longer read using the fusion library methods.
Can I ask what methods/tools the Aroma.Affymetrix package uses to open
and process .CEL files?

Many thanks,
Andy

I don't any one for custom chip typess, but there might be. Have you
checked with dChip?

aroma.affymetrix is using the affxparser package for all Affymetrix
I/O. The affxparser package is an R wrapper on top of the Affymetrix
Fusion SDK. Thus, I am bit puzzled that you have problems. What "the
Fusion com library" are you using, on what platform and language etc.
What is the error message? You say a "handful of files" - not all?

FYI, we don't get any problems so it might be that your version of
Fusion SDK is not working correctly.

Cheers

Henrik
